notes: Migrated from GptNeoxGreedyParityTests. Original provenance: Greedy token parity against llama.cpp for GPT-NeoX (EleutherAI Pythia) — the receipt that admits gptneox to 's architecture allowlist. What GPT-NeoX needs beyond the plain llama trunk — three things, all new to this engine. (1) LayerNorm (mean-subtract + learned scale + learned bias) instead of RMSNorm, on every norm in the model (SimdKernels.LayerNorm, dispatched via ForwardPass.FastNorm whenever is set — detected from tensor inventory, blk.0.attn_norm.bias, the same pattern HasAttnBias uses, not from the architecture string). (2) A non-gated GELU FFN: down(gelu(up(x))), no ffn_gate tensor — SimdKernels.GeluInPlace, the tanh-approximate GELU (0.5*x*(1+tanh(sqrt(2/π)*(x+0.044715*x^3)))), confirmed against ggml/src/ggml-cpu/vec.h's ggml_gelu_f32. DenseFfn/PrefillCore pick this branch over Apertus's xIELU by checking _xieluAlphaN is not null first — the two non-gated activations are mutually exclusive by construction (xIELU needs the unprefixed xielu.alpha_n metadata key that GPT-NeoX GGUFs never declare). (3) Parallel residual (Pythia sets use_parallel_residual=true): attention and FFN both read the SAME pre-attention layer input, and the layer output is a 3-way sum input + attn_out + ffn_out, not two sequential normalize-then-add steps. Implemented as an isolated if (_hp.UseParallelResidual) { ... } else { /* untouched sequential path */ } branch in both RunTrunk (single-token decode) and PrefillCore (batched prefill), so every other architecture's code path is byte-identical to before this work. Also new: GPT-NeoX ships a fused attn_qkv.weight/attn_qkv.bias (2304-wide) rather than separate attn_q/attn_k/attn_v tensors — ForwardPass's constructor splits the fused tensor by byte/row offset for the weight and by element offset for the bias. One real defect found and fixed building this receipt — caught by the oracle-free stepwise test, not by inspection. PrefillCore's final output-norm (both the last-token-only path and the diagnostic onAllPositionLogits path) still called SimdKernels.RmsNorm directly, never updated to the new bias-aware FastNorm dispatcher — RunTrunk's equivalent final norm WAS updated. Symptom: the greedy-continuation test below (argmax-only assertions) passed regardless, because omitting a per-channel additive bias before the output projection shifts every position's logits by the same outputWeight × bias vector, which generally does not reorder the top candidates — a fluent, plausible-looking pass that was hiding a real bug, the exact standing risk this plan's evidence rule exists for. GptNeox_DecodeStepwise_AgreesWithSinglePassPrefill caught it immediately: prefill-in-one-call vs prefill-then-decode disagreed by 261.6 on raw logit magnitude despite computing the identical argmax at every position (confirmed via a temporary per-position argmax dump before touching any code, which is what pointed at "same decisions, different scale" rather than a routing/attention bug). Fixed by routing both call sites through FastNorm. Partial RoPE needed one small new dispatch; the epsilon key needed none. gptneox.rope.dimension_count=16 (headDim is 64) — is already read generically from {arch}.rope.dimension_count (originally added for qwen35moe), confirmed via the Assert.Equal(16, hp.RopeDim) guard below. But ForwardPass.ApplyRopeLayer (shared by RunTrunk and PrefillCore) always rotated the full headDim — harmless for every prior architecture, where RopeDim == headDim, but wrong here. Fixed by adding a _ropeDim field and dispatching to SimdKernels.ApplyRoPECachedNeoxPartial (already existed, built earlier for qwen35moe's hybrid forward pass, but never called from the plain CPU dense path) whenever _ropeDim < headDim. RmsNormEps already falls back from {arch}.attention.layer_norm_rms_epsilon (absent for GPT-NeoX) to {arch}.attention.layer_norm_epsilon (GPT-NeoX's actual key, 1e-5 on this checkpoint) with no new code needed — confirmed the real key is read, not the coincidentally-matching fallback constant, by reading the key-selection logic in ModelGraph.cs directly. RoPE convention. NEOX (pairs offset by headDim/2), confirmed directly against llama_model_rope_type() in examples/llama.cpp/llama.cpp/src/llama-model.cpp (LLM_ARCH_GPTNEOX falls into the LLAMA_ROPE_TYPE_NEOX case block) and independently cross-checked against this checkpoint's own llama-completion startup log, which prints rope type = 2 (NEOX) for this exact GGUF. QKV layout — a third-party review's claim was checked against source and found wrong. A review of an earlier draft of this work (not authored by, or verified against source by, its author) asserted the fused attn_qkv tensor was laid out interleaved per head (Q0,K0,V0,Q1,K1,V1,...). Checked directly against examples/llama.cpp/llama.cpp/conversion/gptneox.py (which reshapes and torch.cats Q/K/V rows into a plain contiguous block) and src/models/gptneox.cpp's build_qkv before any code was written against the claim: the layout is contiguous (all Q rows, then all K rows, then all V rows), not interleaved. The fused-tensor split in ForwardPass's constructor uses the verified layout. A fabricated-looking-but-wrong value found and fixed while writing this receipt. An earlier draft of the stepwise-agreement test below used token ids 3422/287 for the two tokens appended after the prompt, without having actually run llama-tokenize to derive them. Re-deriving them directly (llama-tokenize -p "The capital of France is located" → ids end in 4441; -p "...located in" → ids end in 4441, 275) showed the draft's values were wrong (they decode to unrelated tokens, not " located"/" in") — every id below was re-derived from a live llama-tokenize run, not carried over from the draft. Checkpoint. EleutherAI/pythia-160m (Apache-2.0), via mradermacher/pythia-160m-GGUF, Q8_0 (174.6 MB, deleted after this receipt). tokenizer.ggml.pre = olmo — already covered by the existing pretokenizer cascade; tokenizer.ggml.model = gpt2 (byte-BPE), so this exercises the architecture axis only, not tokenizer code. Reference. tools/llama.cpp build b8585-cad2d3884: llama-tokenize -m <model> -p "The capital of France is" --ids --no-bos -> [510, 5347, 273, 6181, 310] llama-completion -m <model> -p "The capital of France is" -n 24 --temp 0 --top-k 1 --seed 0 \ -no-cnv --override-kv tokenizer.ggml.add_bos_token=bool:false -> "The capital of France is located in the city of Paris. The city is also home to the famous French football club, the Paris Saint" Result: 22 of 24 tokens EXACT, stronger than every prior receipt this session (Apertus 11/24, OLMoE 2-token prefix). The engine's greedy continuation matches llama.cpp token-for-token through " located in the city of Paris.\n\nThe city is also home to the famous French football club, the " (steps 0-21, verified via below) and diverges only at the last two tokens. Accepted on the same basis as the OLMoE and Apertus receipts (see docs/done/01-gguf-model-coverage-plan.md §1b, §1f): a divergence this late, on this strong a prefix, after independently verifying every structural claim above against llama.cpp source rather than a third party's summary of it, reads as ordinary Q8_0 accumulation-order sensitivity rather than a remaining structural bug.
